cves.description: In Eclipse Ditto versions 1.1.0 to 3.9.8, when pre-authentication is enabled, the gateway service accepts the pre-authenticated subject not only from the `x-ditto-pre-authenticated` HTTP header set by a trusted reverse proxy, but also from an undocumented `x-ditto-pre-authenticated` URL query parameter that a client can set. A reverse proxy that only overwrites the header therefore does not stop clients from supplying their own subject. With the default configuration of the Ditto Helm chart (`global.jwtOnly: false`, which implicitly enables pre-authentication), the bundled nginx skips HTTP Basic authentication for any request with an `Authorization: Bearer` header and forwards it without the pre-authentication header. An unauthenticated remote attacker can send an invalid Bearer token together with the query parameter to authenticate as any chosen policy subject. Pre-authentication succeeds before the JWT is validated, so the attacker can read and modify Things and Policies with that subject's permissions. As a mitigation, disable pre-authentication in the gateway (`ENABLE_PRE_AUTHENTICATION=false`) or, when using the Helm chart, configure `global.jwtOnly: true`.

PHP-FPM request smuggling through an unread HTTP request body.

PHP does not discard the unread part of an HTTP request body at request shutdown when the application has opened php://input without reading it to the end. When the front end reuses backend connections, which is not the default in nginx or Apache (for example nginx with fastcgi_keep_conn on, or Apache mod_proxy_fcgi with enablereuse=on), PHP-FPM can parse the leftover bytes as a new FastCGI request. An unauthenticated remote attacker can use a single crafted multipart/form-data request to forge a backend request with chosen parameters such as SCRIPT_FILENAME, REMOTE_ADDR and PHP_ADMIN_VALUE, which can lead to execution of attacker-controlled PHP code. With LSAPI, subsequent requests on the connection can be disrupted.

This issue affects PHP versions before 8.2.36, 8.3.* before 8.3.37, 8.4.* before 8.4.28 and 8.5.* before 8.5.13.

PHP-FPM epoll use-after-free can lead to local privilege escalation.

When catch_workers_output is enabled and the epoll event backend is used, the PHP-FPM master can close a worker's output pipe in fpm_child_close() without removing the associated event, and the delayed cleanup can free the worker record while its epoll registration is still active. A later event is then dispatched through a pointer into freed memory. A local attacker who can execute PHP code in an FPM worker can crash the master or execute code with its privileges, commonly root. catch_workers_output is disabled by default but enabled in the official PHP-FPM Docker images.

This issue affects PHP versions from 8.1.20 through 8.1.34, from 8.2.7 before 8.2.36, 8.3.* before 8.3.37, 8.4.* before 8.4.28 and 8.5.* before 8.5.13.

PHP-FPM status endpoint XSS via unescaped user and script fields.

The PHP-FPM full status output includes the request method, authentication user and script filename of each worker without escaping them for the HTML, XML or JSON format. When the status endpoint is enabled, an unauthenticated remote attacker can store markup in a worker's scoreboard entry with an ordinary request, for example through the username of an HTTP Basic authentication header that the web server forwards to PHP-FPM, or through the script filename where the attacker can influence it. When a user views the full status page as HTML, the injected JavaScript runs in the origin of that page. The attacker does not need access to the status endpoint. Malformed XML or JSON output can also disrupt monitoring tools.

This issue affects PHP versions before 8.2.36, 8.3.* before 8.3.37, 8.4.* before 8.4.28 and 8.5.* before 8.5.13.

modified eCommerce Shopsoftware through 3.3.0 contains a stored cross-site scripting vulnerability that allows authenticated administrators to inject scripts via the unsanitized products_model field. Attackers with product editing permission can store JavaScript that executes in browsers of other administrators, storefront visitors, and customers viewing carts and order history.

Tiptap @tiptap/core 2.0.0-alpha.0 before 3.30.4 contains a cross-site scripting vulnerability that allows attackers to inject DOM attributes via a __proto__ key passed to mergeAttributes(). Attackers can supply untrusted JSON attribute data whose __proto__ replaces the merged object's prototype, causing DOMSerializer.renderSpec to render injected event handlers that execute JavaScript.

WatchAlert 2.0.0 through 3.9.20 contains an insecure direct object reference vulnerability in the /api/w8t/datasource/dataSourceGet endpoint that lets authenticated users read other tenants' datasources because lookups omit tenant_id filtering. Tenant members with datasource view permission can request another tenant's datasource ID to obtain basic auth passwords, AWS and Alibaba Cloud keys, and Kubernetes kubeconfigs.

parse5 7.0.0 before 8.1.1 contains an uncaught exception vulnerability in Preprocessor#_processSurrogate that allows remote attackers to crash applications by supplying two consecutive low surrogates. Attackers can submit input such as U+DC00 U+DC00, which decodes to out-of-range code point 0x110000 and throws a RangeError from parse, parseFragment, or streaming parsers, crashing Node.js processes.

@scalar/typebox before 0.1.4 contains a code injection vulnerability in TypeCompiler that allows attackers to execute JavaScript by supplying crafted schema strings. Attackers can inject single-quote breakouts into string format, Kind names, property keys or Literal values to run arbitrary JavaScript in the host Node.js process during Compile() and Check().

InfoScan fails to properly handle certain malformed or incomplete requests to its login and password-reset endpoints. These requests can trigger unhandled server exceptions that return detailed Node.js stack traces to the requester. The responses disclose internal filesystem paths, application directory names, source file locations, and line numbers.

NLTK (Natural Language Toolkit) is a suite of open source Python modules, data sets, and tutorials supporting research and development in Natural Language Processing. From 3.10.3 until 3.10.4, the NLTK 3.10.3 JVM hardening validates Java launcher tokens in the options channel but appends the caller-controlled cmd sequence without requiring its first token to be a main class. Supplying -jar or an @argfile through nltk.internals.java or StanfordSegmenter.java_class can therefore execute attacker-selected Java bytecode without the unsafe-JAR opt-in. This issue is fixed in version 3.10.4.

A flaw was found in Keycloak. An authenticated remote user with a pending required security action, such as configuring multi-factor authentication (MFA), can bypass the mandatory action by submitting a specially crafted request to the consent endpoint without a valid session code. Keycloak incorrectly interprets the submission as a page refresh and completes the authentication process, allowing the user to access the application without fulfilling the required security policies.

pREST (PostgreSQL REST) is an API that delivers an application on top of a Postgres database. Prior to 2.4.0, the vulnerable parameter is _groupby, handled by GroupByClause in adapters/postgres/postgres.go. adapters/postgres/postgres.go uses the weaker isSafeSQLExpression check for this function-expression branch instead of the stricter single-field validator used for _select. That check validates only the outer function name against a 13-function allowlist and permits nested subqueries, trailing UNION syntax, and inner pg_ functions. controllers/crud.go concatenates the GROUP BY expression while parameterizing only WHERE values, allowing attacker-controlled SQL structure into the clause. Default configuration permits unauthenticated access; a restricted installation may require a low-privilege table reader. UNION-based extraction requires compatible column counts and types and was not verified end to end, but a delay-producing function can cause denial of service without that alignment. This issue is fixed in 2.4.0.

@fastify/http-proxy is a Fastify plugin that proxies HTTP and WebSocket traffic to an upstream server. In versions before 11.6.10, it rejects destinations containing parent-directory path segments by an exact string match, so a segment that carries a semicolon path parameter, such as a dot-dot segment followed by a semicolon and an optional parameter, is not equal to the plain dot-dot form and passes the check, and the WHATWG URL parser keeps it as an ordinary segment so the rewrite-prefix containment check also passes. Servlet containers such as Apache Tomcat and Jetty strip semicolon path parameters from each segment before resolving dot-segments, so a request routed through the configured prefix is rewritten and reaches the upstream where it resolves above the intended subtree, escaping the path the proxy is meant to expose and, on some containers, crossing application contexts. Both the HTTP and WebSocket proxy paths are affected. The issue is fixed in @fastify/http-proxy 11.6.10, and users should upgrade to 11.6.10 or later.

@fastify/reply-from is a Fastify plugin that forwards requests to an upstream HTTP server. In versions before 12.8.4, its buildURL function rejects parent-directory path segments by an exact string match, so a segment that carries a semicolon path parameter, such as a dot-dot segment followed by a semicolon and an optional parameter, is not equal to the plain dot-dot form and passes the traversal check, and the WHATWG URL parser keeps it as an ordinary segment so the base-prefix containment check also passes. Backends that strip semicolon path parameters before resolving dot-segments, such as Apache Tomcat, Jetty, WildFly, and Spring Boot, turn the segment back into a parent-directory reference and resolve it, so an unauthenticated client can escape the intended upstream prefix and reach internal paths such as admin or internal API endpoints, including with state-changing methods. Deployments that proxy to Node.js, nginx, or Express upstreams are not affected. The issue is fixed in @fastify/reply-from 12.8.4, and users should upgrade to 12.8.4 or later.

@fastify/http-proxy is a Fastify plugin that proxies HTTP and WebSocket traffic to an upstream server. In versions from 9.0.0 up to but not including 11.6.10, when the plugin is registered with websocket support enabled, it takes every upgraded socket and dispatches the request through the Fastify router before the WebSocket library takes ownership of the socket. Node.js removes its own error listener from the socket before emitting the upgrade event, and the plugin does not attach one of its own during routing, so a socket error such as a client connection reset that arrives before the WebSocket library takes over is unhandled and terminates the Node.js process. The error window is open whenever anything asynchronous runs between dispatch and the route handler, such as an async hook on the proxied route or any unrelated async route in the application. A single unauthenticated upgrade request followed by a connection reset is enough to crash the server, and it can be repeated to keep the process down. The issue is fixed in @fastify/http-proxy 11.6.10, and users should upgrade to 11.6.10 or later.

@fastify/http-proxy is a Fastify plugin that proxies HTTP and WebSocket traffic to an upstream server. In versions from 9.4.0 up to but not including 11.6.10, when the plugin is registered with websocket support enabled, a WebSocket upgrade request whose path carries a URL fragment is matched by the router and answered with a successful upgrade before the upstream link is created. Building the upstream target then throws, the error is only logged, and the accepted client socket is left open with no error listener, so the next frame the client sends becomes an unhandled error and terminates the Node.js process. A request target that is not a valid URL reference reaching a parameterized prefix triggers the same path. A single unauthenticated upgrade request followed by one frame is enough to crash the server, and it can be repeated to keep the process down. The issue is fixed in @fastify/http-proxy 11.6.10, and users should upgrade to 11.6.10 or later.

RepoManager is a self-hosted deb/rpm package repository. Prior to 5.13.3, a registered host or a party with its host/API credential can submit package metadata. Inventory reporting accepts package name and version, while available-update reporting accepts package name, version, and repository; the repository field exists only on that path. RepoManager stores these values, and stored values are rendered on the host's package detail page without preventing stored HTML or JavaScript from executing. An administrator must later view the page for script execution. The script runs in the administrator's authenticated browser session and can expose administrative data or forge privileged requests; the advisory describes possible escalation through admin-only functionality. Fixed in 5.13.3.

@fastify/http-proxy is a Fastify plugin that proxies HTTP and WebSocket traffic to an upstream server. In versions from 9.0.0 up to but not including 11.6.10, when the plugin is registered with websocket support enabled, a WebSocket upgrade that is pipelined behind another HTTP request on the same cleartext connection arrives while that request's response is still attached to the socket. The shared upgrade listener sees the socket is already claimed and returns early without taking the upgrade, but it does not attach an error listener to the raw socket, and Node.js has already removed its own error listener before emitting the upgrade event. A later socket error on that connection, such as a client connection reset, is therefore unhandled and terminates the Node.js process. A single unauthenticated connection that pipelines an upgrade behind a normal request and then resets is enough to crash the server, and it can be repeated to keep the process down. Upgrades over TLS are not affected. The issue is fixed in @fastify/http-proxy 11.6.10, and users should upgrade to 11.6.10 or later.

A reflected Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) vulnerability in WatchGuard Dimension's Device Configuration History page allows an authenticated attacker with view permission on a device to execute arbitrary JavaScript in another authenticated user's browser by enticing the victim to open a specially crafted link.

OpenRemote is an open-source internet-of-things platform. Prior to 1.31.0, an authenticated user who obtains another user's MQTT session ID can disconnect that session across realm boundaries through the GET route GET {realm}/disconnect/{sessionID}. In manager/src/main/java/org/openremote/manager/security/UserResourceImpl.java, disconnectUserSession ignores the requested realm and calls mqttBrokerService.disconnectSession(sessionID) without checking session ownership; model/src/main/java/org/openremote/model/security/UserResource.java exposes the route without an @RolesAllowed restriction. The earlier cross-realm read-method guards did not cover this disconnect method, and same-realm users can also disconnect sessions they do not own. Session IDs are not trivially brute-forceable but may be exposed through monitoring, logs, or correlated API calls, and the unauthorized disconnect can disrupt MQTT connectivity across tenant boundaries without directly disclosing session data. This issue is fixed in 1.31.0.

The MongoDB Node.js Driver does not neutralize NUL characters in the user name and password values it places into the message it builds for SASL PLAIN authentication. A party who can choose the login values that an application passes to the driver can alter where the fields of that message begin and end. This may result in a receiving system reading a login name and secret that differ from the values the application supplied. Authenticating as a different account still requires that account's password. Only deployments that use SASL PLAIN authentication are affected.

A weakness in the MongoDB Node.js driver can place sensitive information taken from an application-supplied connection string into the text of an error produced while that connection string is being parsed. The error is generated inside the application process before any database connection is made, so no database account and no network access are needed for it to occur. A party able to read the application's error output or log files may thereby obtain database credentials that the application's configuration source would otherwise keep to a narrower audience.

In Splunk Enterprise versions below 10.4.4, 10.2.8, 10.0.11, and 9.4.16, a low-privileged user who holds the "power" Splunk role could inject malicious content into a Splunk Web view. When another authenticated user opens the affected view in Splunk Web, the injected content executes unauthorized JavaScript code within the viewing user's browser session.
The vulnerability is possible because Splunk Web does not properly validate content in a view definition before rendering the view.
For more information see Define roles on the Splunk platform with capabilities (https://help.splunk.com/en/splunk-enterprise/administer/manage-users-and-security/10.2/manage-splunk-platform-users-and-roles/define-roles-on-the-splunk-platform-with-capabilities) in the Splunk documentation.

In Splunk Enterprise Security versions below 8.7.0, an unauthenticated user with network-path interception capability could cause attacker-controlled JavaScript to run in the browser of a security analyst who previews a Portable Document Format (PDF) attachment in Mission Control. The JavaScript could expose data and perform actions available to the security analyst.
The vulnerability is possible because Mission Control loads the PDF rendering worker from an external content delivery network.
The vulnerability requires the unauthenticated user to intercept the network path to the external content delivery network and a security analyst to preview a PDF attachment in Mission Control. The unauthenticated user should not be able to exploit the vulnerability at will.
For more information see Collaborate on investigations in Splunk Enterprise Security (https://help.splunk.com/en/splunk-enterprise-security-8/administer/8.7/investigations/collaborate-on-investigations-in-splunk-enterprise-security) in the Splunk documentation.

In Splunk SOAR versions below 8.8.0, a user with edit permission for a container or workbook task could store attacker-controlled Hypertext Markup Language (HTML) in a note. When another user with view permission for the affected container and its notes opens the affected note in Mission Control, the note could run unauthorized JavaScript code in the browser of that user, expose data available through the authenticated session, and perform actions available through the authenticated session.
The vulnerability is possible because Splunk SOAR does not neutralize active content in all notes before Mission Control renders them.

In Splunk SOAR versions below 8.8.0, a user with the containers:edit permission could import a container that includes a malicious Hypertext Markup Language (HTML) note. When another user views the imported note, Splunk SOAR could run unauthorized JavaScript in the browser of that user, exposing data and allowing actions available to that user.
The vulnerability is possible because Splunk SOAR does not sanitize HTML note content during container import before it renders the content in Mission Control.

In Splunk SOAR versions below 8.8.0, a user with container edit permission could supply timestamps when creating containers and artifacts through the Representational State Transfer (REST) API. This could alter the timeline shown to analysts and cause configured data retention strategies to delete affected records earlier than intended.
The vulnerability is possible because the REST API accepts client-supplied values for timestamps that Splunk SOAR uses to order records and apply data retention.
The early deletion impact requires an applicable data retention strategy; the timeline impact does not.
For more information see Manage your PostgreSQL database with data retention strategies (https://help.splunk.com/en/splunk-soar/soar-on-premises/administer-soar-on-premises/6.4.0/manage-your-splunk-soar-on-premises-system-health-and-performance/manage-your-postgresql-database-with-data-retention-strategies) in the Splunk documentation.

Connaisseur is an admission controller that integrates container image signature verification into a Kubernetes cluster. Prior to 3.11.1, the Cosign validator counts valid signature layers rather than distinct trust roots for trustRoot: "*" policies using an explicit threshold or an implicit require-all policy. An attacker who controls one configured trust root's signing key and can attach multiple signatures to an image can satisfy a threshold intended to require multiple independent roots, causing admission without the intended signer quorum. Policies using a single trust root or the required option are not affected. This issue is fixed in 3.11.1.

A component of the MongoDB Java Driver that processes connection configuration places credential values taken from that configuration into generated text and error output without replacing them with a placeholder, unlike other parts of the driver. A party able to read output produced by an application that embeds the driver may obtain database or proxy credentials in clear text.

The MongoDB Java driver applies its DNS seedlist domain restriction to a record value that is later re-interpreted differently when the connection target is parsed, so the name that is checked and the name that is used can differ. An unauthenticated party who can set or forge the DNS service record for the seed domain in a connection string can cause the driver to direct its session to an unrelated host and to complete certificate verification against that host instead. This may result in unintended disclosure of application data and of configured database credentials, and in unintended content being returned to the application as query results.

The MongoDB Java Driver does not neutralize NUL characters in the user name and password values it places into the message it builds for SASL PLAIN authentication. A party who can choose the login values that an application passes to the driver can alter where the fields of that message begin and end. This may result in a receiving system reading a login name and secret that differ from the values the application supplied. Authenticating as a different account still requires that account's password. Only deployments that use SASL PLAIN authentication are affected.

A flaw was found in Keycloak. This vulnerability allows an authenticated remote attacker to cause a denial of service by terminating active sessions of arbitrary users. When processing Security Assertion Markup Language (SAML) documents that lack a root signature, Keycloak accepts the request as long as any assertion within the document is signed, without verifying its context or placement. An attacker holding a validly signed assertion can embed it into an unsigned logout request for another user, causing Keycloak to accept the forged request and terminate the victim's session.

netty-incubator-codec-ohttp implements Oblivious HTTP (OHTTP) gateway and client functionality using Netty. Prior to 0.0.23.Final, BoringSSLAsymmetricCipherKeyPair.toString in codec-ohttp-hpke-classes-boringssl/src/main/java/io/netty/incubator/codec/hpke/boringssl/BoringSSLAsymmetricCipherKeyPair.java includes its private parameter, BoringSSLAsymmetricKeyParameter.toString in codec-ohttp-hpke-classes-boringssl/src/main/java/io/netty/incubator/codec/hpke/boringssl/BoringSSLAsymmetricKeyParameter.java renders the complete private-key byte array when isPrivate is true, and BoringSSL.EVP_HPKE_KEY_init_or_throw in codec-ohttp-hpke-classes-boringssl/src/main/java/io/netty/incubator/codec/hpke/boringssl/BoringSSL.java includes rejected privateKeyBytes in an exception message. Applications that log affected key-pair objects or initialization exceptions can persist complete HPKE private key material in logs or telemetry. Anyone who can read those records can recover the key and may compromise OHTTP message confidentiality or authenticity expectations while the key remains usable. This issue is fixed in version 0.0.23.Final.

netty-incubator-codec-ohttp implements Oblivious HTTP (OHTTP) gateway and client functionality using Netty. Prior to 0.0.23.Final, BinaryHttpParser in codec-bhttp/src/main/java/io/netty/incubator/codec/bhttp/BinaryHttpParser.java accumulates attacker-controlled Binary HTTP variable-length integers into the int offset sumBytes. BinaryHttpParser.readRequestHead, BinaryHttpParser.readFieldLine, and BinaryHttpParser.getIndeterminateLength can narrow long lengths into that offset, causing integer wraparound before buffer indices are calculated. A remote peer that supplies a valid large encoded length to BinaryHttpParser or BinaryHttpDecoder can trigger an unchecked bounds exception from a small malformed message, fail or close the channel, and repeatedly cause denial of service. Java and Netty bounds checks prevent memory corruption, and no information disclosure was observed. This issue is fixed in version 0.0.23.Final.

netty-incubator-codec-ohttp implements Oblivious HTTP (OHTTP) gateway and client functionality using Netty. Prior to 0.0.23.Final, BinaryHttpParser.readFieldLine in codec-bhttp/src/main/java/io/netty/incubator/codec/bhttp/BinaryHttpParser.java treats a complete field line that ends exactly at a known field-section boundary as incomplete and returns without consuming bytes. BinaryHttpParser.readFieldSection then leaves fieldSectionLength unchanged and repeats the loop because its forward-progress checks are Java assertions, which are normally disabled in production. A remote peer that sends a known-length Binary HTTP header or trailer section ending at that boundary can make the parser spin indefinitely and pin the Netty event-loop or worker thread responsible for the channel. This issue is fixed in version 0.0.23.Final.

netty-incubator-codec-ohttp implements Oblivious HTTP (OHTTP) gateway and client functionality using Netty. Prior to 0.0.23.Final, BinaryHttpParser.readFieldSection in codec-bhttp/src/main/java/io/netty/incubator/codec/bhttp/BinaryHttpParser.java loops while fieldSectionLength is nonzero and relies on disabled-by-default assertions to require BinaryHttpParser.readFieldLine to return a value and consume bytes. A corrupt field line can consume more bytes than its understated declared section length and drive the counter negative, or a truncated field line can return without consuming data and leave the parser in the same state. An unauthenticated OHTTP peer can encrypt such Binary HTTP content under the gateway public configuration, reach OHttpRequestResponseContext.ContentDecoder.decodeChunk, and permanently pin a Netty event-loop thread at full CPU before application business logic. Multiple requests can exhaust the event-loop group and deny service until restart. This issue is fixed in version 0.0.23.Final.

netty-incubator-codec-ohttp implements Oblivious HTTP (OHTTP) gateway and client functionality using Netty. From 0.0.20.Final until 0.0.27.Final, OHttpClientCodec in codec-ohttp/src/main/java/io/netty/incubator/codec/ohttp/OHttpClientCodec.java and OHttpServerCodec in codec-ohttp/src/main/java/io/netty/incubator/codec/ohttp/OHttpServerCodec.java retain the consumed outer cumulationBuffer after a valid OHTTP exchange completes, even though OHttpRequestResponseContext.destroy in codec-ohttp/src/main/java/io/netty/incubator/codec/ohttp/OHttpRequestResponseContext.java releases the inner Binary HTTP cumulation and the channel remains active. A peer can complete a large request or response and leave the keep-alive connection idle, causing the client and server handlers to retain the current high-water pooled or direct buffer capacity until later inbound content replaces it or the handler is removed. Many long-lived idle connections can pin substantial memory and create availability pressure. The issue does not cause unbounded growth for repeated exchanges on a single channel. This issue is fixed in version 0.0.27.Final.

Reliance on obfuscation or encryption of Security-Relevant inputs without integrity checking, Improper validation of integrity check value, Cleartext transmission of sensitive information vulnerability in the EncryptInterceptor of Apache Tomcat.



This issue affects Apache Tomcat: from 11.0.0-M1 through 11.0.27, from 10.1.0-M1 through 10.1.61, from 9.0.13 through 9.0.123.



The following versions were EOL at the time the CVE was created but are known to be affected: from 8.5.38 through 8.5.100, from 7.0.100 through 7.0.109. Other unsupported versions may also be affected.



Users are recommended to upgrade to version 11.0.29, 10.1.62 or 9.0.124 and switch to TLS-PSK to encrypt cluster communication, which fixes the issue.
Note: Tomcat 11.0.28 was not released

A flaw was found in Keycloak. When configured with a database that uses case-insensitive collation, Keycloak resolves realm URLs regardless of letter casing. A remote attacker can exploit this behavior by sending requests with alternate letter casing to bypass upstream reverse proxy access controls that rely on case-sensitive path matching. This issue can expose restricted authentication endpoints intended only for internal access, though Keycloak's internal authentication mechanisms remain intact.

A flaw was found in Keycloak. When an administrator revokes tokens by setting a not-before revocation cutoff, Keycloak fails to enforce this boundary when processing User-Managed Access (UMA) grant requests using ID token claims. An authenticated remote user with an active session can submit a previously revoked ID token to receive a fresh Requesting Party Token (RPT). This flaw allows an attacker to bypass token revocation and retain unauthorized access to protected resources.

A flaw was found in Keycloak. When processing token requests using the User-Managed Access (UMA) grant, Keycloak fails to verify whether a target client or resource server is enabled before issuing an authorization token. An authenticated remote user can exploit this flaw to obtain valid Requesting Party Tokens (RPTs) for disabled clients, bypassing administrative access controls and permissions restrictions.

A flaw was found in Keycloak. The Account API endpoint for sharing resources fails to verify whether owner-managed access is enabled and accepts permission scopes not assigned to the resource. An authenticated user can exploit this vulnerability to generate pre-granted permission tickets, causing Keycloak to bypass policy evaluation and issue access tokens with unauthorized scopes.

A flaw was found in Keycloak. When a client application enforces step-up authentication or multi-factor authentication (MFA) via a minimum authentication level, Keycloak fails to apply this requirement to login sessions initiated through the credential reset endpoint. An attacker who possesses a user's initial credentials (such as a password) can navigate from the reset interface back to the standard login form and authenticate without completing the required second factor. This flaw allows an attacker to obtain valid access tokens and gain unauthorized access to protected services without satisfying mandatory security controls.

A security flaw has been discovered in sofastack sofa-bolt up to 1.6.12. Affected by this issue is the function HessianSerializer.deserialize of the file src/main/java/com/alipay/remoting/serialization/HessianSerializer.java of the component Hessian2 Deserialization. Performing a manipulation results in allocation of resources. The attack can be initiated remotely. The vendor was contacted early about this disclosure but did not respond in any way.

A weakness has been identified in sofastack sofa-bolt up to 1.6.12. This impacts the function initSSLContext of the file src/main/java/com/alipay/remoting/connection/AbstractConnectionFactory.java of the component TLS Stack. Executing a manipulation can lead to certificate with host mismatch. The attack may be performed from remote. This attack is characterized by high complexity. The exploitability is said to be difficult. The vendor was contacted early about this disclosure but did not respond in any way.

A flaw was found in Keycloak. The OpenID Connect (OIDC) logout endpoint continues to honor post-logout redirect rules for disabled clients rather than rejecting the requests. If a disabled client retains permissive redirect configurations, a remote attacker can exploit this issue by supplying an arbitrary redirection target in a logout request, leading to an open redirect that can be used in phishing attacks.

A flaw was found in Keycloak. When evaluating access permissions, Keycloak Authorization Services improperly matches resource paths containing wildcard file extensions by evaluating only the file extension suffix and ignoring configured path prefixes. An authenticated remote attacker could exploit this vulnerability by requesting a restricted resource that shares a file extension with a more permissive resource, leading to an authorization bypass and unintended access to protected data.

Improper neutralization of special elements in data query logic (Cypher injection) in the orderBy placeholder handling for custom queries in Neo4j Spring Data Neo4j versions 6.1.0 through 8.0.8 and 8.1.0 through 8.1.2 allows a remote attacker to read database contents via blind reads, write read content into new nodes, or, if APOC and APOC file export are enabled, to write query results to a file in the database's accessible file system via crafted sort order parameters. Exploitation requires an application that passes unvalidated user input as the orderBy value to a custom Cypher query using the placeholder directive.

The flowintel Docker build workflow used the GitHub Actions checkout action with default credential persistence, causing the job authentication token to be written into the repository's Git configuration file. This file became part of the Docker build context and could be retained in exported build cache layers, even though Git metadata was stripped from the final runtime image.

An attacker with access to the CI/CD build cache or build environment could extract the persisted token and use it to gain unauthorized access to the private source repository.

Impact:
- Exposure of a valid authentication token to the private repository
- Potential unauthorized read access to source code and repository metadata

Affected versions: flowintel < 4.1.0

Flowintel contains multiple SSO identity and organisation trust boundary violations that collectively allow account takeover, privilege escalation, and unauthorized access to private case data.

- Keycloak SSO accepted unverified email claims, and all SSO providers (Keycloak, Entra ID, SimpleSAML) could resolve a claimed email address to an existing account that was created via a different sign-in method, enabling cross-provider account collision and unauthorized access to another user's account and data.

- Entra ID role mapping relied on group display names, which tenant members could duplicate by creating a group with the same name as a privileged group (e.g. FlowintelAdmin), resulting in unauthorized role escalation.

- SSO provisioning reused organisations whose display names matched user-controlled profile names, granting the new SSO user access to that organisation's private cases without explicit administrator assignment.

- Case sharing via the API resolved organisations by name using a first-match query, so ambiguous names could silently resolve to the wrong organisation.

Preconditions: an attacker must have a valid SSO identity (Keycloak, Entra ID, or SimpleSAML) or be a member of the relevant Entra tenant. No local administrator access is required.

Security impact: unauthorized access to private case data, privilege escalation to Editor or higher roles, and account takeover across authentication providers.

Affected versions: Flowintel prior to 4.1.0.

A vulnerability was found in hiparker opsli-boot up to 2.2.1. This affects the function getInputStream of the file opsli-plugins/opsli-plugins-waf/src/main/java/org/opsli/plugins/waf/servlet/WafHttpServletRequestWrapper.java of the component WAF Plugin. The manipulation results in denial of service. The attack can be executed remotely.

A weakness has been identified in PowerJob up to 5.1.7. This affects the function CustomHttpServletRequestWrapper of the file powerjob-server/powerjob-server-starter/src/main/java/tech/powerjob/server/config/CachingRequestBodyFilter.java of the component CachingRequestBodyFilter. Executing a manipulation can lead to denial of service. It is possible to launch the attack remotely.

A vulnerability was determined in tianshiyeben wgcloud up to 4.0.1. This vulnerability affects unknown code of the file AgentController.java of the component minTask Endpoint. Executing a manipulation can lead to allocation of resources. The attack can be executed remotely.

A vulnerability was identified in OpenZipkin Zipkin 3.6.1. This affects the function UnzippingBytesRequestConverter.convertRequest of the file zipkin-server/src/main/java/zipkin2/server/internal/ZipkinHttpCollector.java of the component HTTP Collector. Such manipulation leads to highly compressed data. The attack can be executed remotely. The pull request to fix this issue awaits acceptance.

Penpot 2.18.0 before 2.18.2 contains a stored cross-site scripting vulnerability that allows authenticated users with edit rights to bypass the sanitize-svg-element blocklist using namespace-prefixed SVG elements. Attackers can upload SVGs containing elements like x:script or attributes like x:onload, which are served inline as image/svg+xml to run JavaScript in victims' Penpot sessions.

A vulnerability was found in erupts erupt up to 2.0.2. This impacts the function EruptUserController.createCode of the file erupt-upms/src/main/java/xyz/erupt/upms/controller/EruptUserController.java of the component UPMS CAPTCHA Endpoint. Performing a manipulation of the argument height results in uncontrolled memory allocation. The attack may be initiated remotely. Upgrading to version 2.0.3 will fix this issue. The patch is named fc59a6eece991ff5aced363243d0b2d14f73ed95. It is recommended to upgrade the affected component.

In Postgres Enterprise Manager (PEM), the pem_agent role, which every PEM agent login inherits, is a member of the PostgreSQL pg_read_server_files and pg_write_server_files roles on the PEM backend database. An attacker who controls any monitored host, and so its PEM agent certificate, can read and write files on the PEM server host as the postgres operating system user. This includes the PEM certificate authority key, which lets the attacker issue certificates for other agents and act as them.
From PEM 10.6.1, PEM agents no longer hold these roles.

In Postgres Enterprise Manager (PEM), several SECURITY DEFINER functions in the pem schema of the PEM backend database are owned by a superuser but do not set a safe search_path. Any PEM user who can connect to the PEM backend database can create objects that these functions use in place of the intended ones, and so run arbitrary SQL with superuser privileges. Temporary objects can be used for this on every supported PostgreSQL version, and objects in the public schema on PostgreSQL 14 backends and backends upgraded from PostgreSQL 14.
From PEM 10.6.1, these functions run with a fixed search_path.

pmo-platform is a modular PMO and release-management platform for Claude Code. From 3.48 until 3.69.1, release/skills/pmo-skill-refiner/eval-viewer/generate_review.py reads untrusted model or skill output from workspace/run*/outputs/ and embeds it with json.dumps into viewer.html inside an inline script without escaping HTML metacharacters. A crafted output can close the script element and execute JavaScript when an operator generates and opens the viewer. The maintainer also confirmed that DOM-based injection through renderGrades and renderBenchmark innerHTML survives transport-only escaping, so affected render sinks must neutralize the content. Executed script can read embedded prompts and outputs, alter the viewer DOM, or modify saved feedback. This issue is fixed in version 3.69.1.

NukeViet CMS is a multi Content Management System. Prior to 4.5.09, the Comment module accepts attacker-controlled base64 content in the status_comment parameter through modules/comment/funcs/main.php; modules/comment/comment.php decodes it with nv_base64_decode() and assigns it to STATUS_COMMENT without output escaping. The required checkss token was derived from the site-wide NV_CACHE_PREFIX rather than NV_CHECK_SESSION, so a token disclosed in public comment markup could be reused across sessions in a crafted URL. An unauthenticated attacker can therefore cause decoded HTML or JavaScript to render in a victim's browser and perform phishing or same-origin actions. This issue is fixed in version 4.5.09.

NukeViet CMS is a multi Content Management System. From the 4.x release line until 4.5.09, a low-privileged authenticated user can store script-breaking content in the first_name and last_name profile fields used to form a comment display name. Both reply links in themes/default/modules/comment/comment.tpl interpolate {COMMENT.post_name} into the inline onclick call to nv_commment_feedback(). HTML numeric references produced by Request::_get_title() are decoded by the browser before JavaScript parsing, so clicking Reply can terminate the string and execute attacker-controlled JavaScript in the visitor's origin, including an administrator's session. This issue is fixed in version 4.5.09.

NukeViet CMS is a multi Content Management System. Prior to 4.5.09, a user with news-posting permission can bypass NukeViet\Core\Request::filterAttr() by prefixing an event-handler attribute with an ASCII form-feed character, which PHP trimming preserves but browsers treat as whitespace. NukeViet\Core\Request::unhtmlentities() omitted a decimal HTML entity tab embedded in a javascript: URI. These parser differences allow persistent event handlers or script URLs to survive filtering in vendor/vinades/nukeviet/Core/Request.php and execute for visitors, including administrators. This issue is fixed in version 4.5.09.

MapServer is a system for developing web-based GIS applications. Prior to 8.6.5, an unauthenticated reflected cross-site scripting vulnerability in OGC API Features collection-items HTML output allows crafted offset or limit query parameter values from raw CGI request handling in src/mapogcapi.cpp to reach template.params.offset or template.params.limit. share/ogcapi/templates/html-bootstrap/collection-items.html inserts those values without quoting or escaping into a script element. A victim who follows a crafted request can have the script element terminated by attacker-controlled markup, causing arbitrary JavaScript to execute under the MapServer origin and enabling access to browser-session data, actions as the victim, and content manipulation. This issue is fixed in 8.6.5.

MapServer is a system for developing web-based GIS applications. From 6.0 until 8.6.5, MapServer's WMS OpenLayers output, selected by FORMAT=application/openlayers or template=openlayers, substitutes a request-derived online-resource value into a single-quoted JavaScript string in src/maptemplate.c. The prior remediation for GHSA-xqj6-vjqr-33vv used msEscapeJSonLikeString() to protect the JavaScript string but did not neutralize angle brackets, so attacker-controlled X-Forwarded-Host or X-Forwarded-Proto values can still terminate the script element at the HTML parser layer. Deployments that expose attacker-controlled PATH_INFO or map= values reaching the same string are also affected. An unauthenticated attacker can cause arbitrary JavaScript to execute in a victim's browser under the MapServer origin when the victim loads the crafted output. This issue is fixed in version 8.6.5.

MapServer is a system for developing web-based GIS applications. Prior to 8.6.5, MapServer's PostgreSQL JOIN implementation in src/mappostgresql.c copies the source layer attribute selected by JOIN FROM into joininfo->from_value and embeds it without parameterization or escaping into a dynamically generated PostgreSQL query executed by PQexec(). When PostgreSQL JOIN support is enabled, an attacker who can control that source feature attribute can inject quote characters and SQL operators that alter the intended WHERE predicate. This second-order injection can cause unintended rows and JOIN attributes to be returned, potentially exposing information from unrelated PostgreSQL records. This issue is fixed in version 8.6.5.

isomorphic-git is a pure JavaScript implementation of Git for Node.js and browsers. Prior to 1.38.7, tree-entry validation in src/models/GitTree.js does not reject the Windows NTFS reserved pathname alias .git::$INDEX_ALLOCATION. When clone() or checkout materializes an attacker-controlled tree containing this alias on Windows using an NTFS filesystem, the alias resolves to the active .git directory and permits writes to trusted repository metadata instead of a normal worktree directory. A malicious repository or object stream can therefore poison repository configuration, hooks, refs, attributes, or other gitdir state. Strict hosting that rejects hasDotgit objects can block the crafted tree, and non-NTFS systems do not interpret the pathname as the active gitdir. isomorphic-git performs the gitdir write but does not itself execute the written hook or configuration; a later native Git or compatible-tool action, such as processing a poisoned core.fsmonitor value, can execute configured commands as the victim developer or CI identity. This issue is fixed in version 1.38.7.

isomorphic-git is a pure JavaScript implementation of Git for Node.js and browsers. Prior to 1.38.8, git cherry-pick applies tree changes through applyTreeChanges in src/utils/walkerToTreeEntryMap.js without checking whether a leading path component is a symbolic link. If a victim worktree contains a tracked symlink to a location outside the worktree and a cherry-picked tree places a file beneath that path, the write follows the symlink and materializes attacker-controlled blob content at the external destination. This allows arbitrary file writes and can cause data tampering, code injection into interpreted files, privilege escalation, denial of service, or follow-on code execution depending on the selected target path. This issue is fixed in version 1.38.8.

NukeViet CMS is a multi Content Management System. Prior to 4.6.01, an unauthenticated visitor can submit Contact module content containing numeric HTML entities with more than eight leading zeros in a URL-bearing attribute. NukeViet\Core\Request::unhtmlentities() does not decode that form before filterAttr() checks for a javascript: scheme, but browsers decode it when rendering the stored content. With an allowed tag such as the default iframe, the reconstructed script URL executes in the administration origin when staff view the message, permitting session-riding actions while remaining unable to read the HttpOnly session cookie directly. This issue is fixed in version 4.6.01.

NukeViet CMS is a multi Content Management System. From the 3.x release line until 4.6.01, an unauthenticated visitor can submit a Contact module message containing an event-handler attribute prefixed by a slash. NukeViet\Core\Request::filterTags() tokenizes attributes using only ASCII spaces, so it sees /onerror and misses the ^on denylist, while the browser treats the slash as a separator and activates onerror. The message is stored and rendered without output encoding in the administration panel, which lacks a Content Security Policy, allowing same-origin JavaScript execution when an administrator opens the message. This issue is fixed in version 4.6.01.

NukeViet CMS is a multi Content Management System. Prior to 4.5.12 and 4.6.02, an attacker who can reach an image-upload flow can upload a valid image with appended PHP short-tag code and a double-extension filename. NukeViet\Files\Upload::save_file() relied on verify_image(), which missed the <? short-open tag, while filename handling preserved embedded dots, validation inspected only the final extension, and an .htaccess rule blocked PHP extensions only at the end of the URI. On Apache mod_php systems configured with short_open_tag and a PHP extension handler, the stored polyglot can execute as PHP and run operating-system commands as the web-server user; PHP-FPM, nginx, and end-anchored handler configurations are not exposed to the execution step. This issue is fixed in versions 4.5.12 and 4.6.02.

NukeViet CMS is a multi Content Management System. From 4.5.08 until 4.5.12 and 4.6.02, an attacker can place NukeViet's internal {@[, ]@}, [@{, and }@] sanitizer markers in an iframe srcdoc value by encoding square brackets as HTML entities. Recursive NukeViet\Core\Request::filterTags() processing decodes the characters, accepts the forged marker, and later converts it to real markup without normal tag or attribute filtering. Because an unsandboxed srcdoc iframe shares the parent origin and iframe is enabled by default through NV_ALLOWED_HTML_TAGS, stored Contact messages, comments with the editor enabled, or submitted articles can execute JavaScript with the viewer's session. This issue is fixed in versions 4.5.12 and 4.6.02.

NukeViet CMS is a multi Content Management System. From 4.5.00 until 4.5.13 and 4.6.02, an unauthenticated attacker can place a multiply encoded value in the news module search q parameter. $nv_Request->get_title() decodes and sanitizes the input once, but modules/news/funcs/search.php subsequently applies urldecode() after sanitization. The resulting raw keyword reaches the {KEY} search-input attribute through search_theme() and the no-results element through search_result_theme() in the default and mobile themes, permitting attribute or tag injection and same-origin JavaScript execution when a victim opens the crafted search URL. This issue is fixed in versions 4.5.13 and 4.6.02.

U.S Department of the Interior Unstable Slope Management Program allows attackers with valid local application credentials to establish an application session by sending JSON POST requests to the application's login endpoint without a Referrer header or completing the intended Keycloak flow. Fixed on or around 2026-10-19.

MaxKB is an open-source AI assistant for enterprise. Prior to 2.10.7-lts, custom Tool Init Param definitions accept attacker-controlled props_info.rules[].validator strings through POST /admin/api/workspace/{workspace_id}/tool and PUT /admin/api/workspace/{workspace_id}/tool/{tool_id}, store them without restriction, and pass them to eval() when the parameter form renders. An authenticated user with the default USER workspace role can store JavaScript and trigger execution by opening the tool's Debug screen before entering or submitting a parameter value. The same Init Param form is exposed to accounts with edit permission on the tool, but execution by a different account was not independently verified. The confirmed script runs in the MaxKB origin; access to another user's bearer token and authenticated account authority is plausible only if that user renders the malicious form. This issue is fixed in version 2.10.7-lts.

LibreChat is an enhanced ChatGPT clone that supports multiple AI providers. Prior to 0.8.9, GET /api/permissions/search-principals passes the q parameter to JavaScript RegExp construction and MongoDB regex queries in packages/data-schemas/src/methods/userGroup.ts findGroupsByNamePattern and searchPrincipals without escaping metacharacters. An authenticated user with people-picker permission can submit a catastrophic-backtracking pattern that blocks the Node.js event loop and makes the service unresponsive to concurrent users; invalid patterns can also produce server errors. This issue is fixed in version 0.8.9.

OceanWP WordPress Theme before 4.2.9 contains a stored cross-site scripting vulnerability in the oceanwp_edd_terms_list() function in inc/edd/edd-helpers.php, which allows authenticated users with EDD download category creation permissions to inject malicious JavaScript by crafting a category name that breaks out of an unescaped HTML title attribute. Attackers can create a category name containing an event-handler payload that executes in the browser of visitors who interact with the category link on the public EDD archive page, potentially compromising an administrator's session if they view the affected page while authenticated.

probe-image-size before 7.5.0 contains an algorithmic-complexity denial of service vulnerability in lib/exif_utils.js that allows remote unauthenticated attackers to exhaust CPU by supplying self-referencing EXIF IFDs. Attackers can submit a crafted 9.6 KB JPEG with repeated ExifIFD and InteropIFD pointers to block the Node.js event loop for about 23 seconds.

A stored cross-site scripting (XSS) vulnerability exists in the Icon API: Menu submodule of the Drupal 7 Icon API module. When a menu item is configured with the Title Wrapper option enabled, the value of the Title Wrapper Class field is output directly into an HTML attribute without sanitization or escaping. A user with the "administer menu icons" permission can inject a payload such as `title" onmouseover="alert(document.cookie)` that is rendered verbatim on every page displaying the affected menu item, executing arbitrary JavaScript in the browser of any user who interacts with the menu link. This can lead to session theft, account hijacking, and further attacks against site users.

This issue affects Icon API 7.1.0.

The Forminator Forms – Contact Form, Payment Form & Custom Form Builder plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'upload-1 (the File Upload field's element_id)' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 1.58.4 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. This vulnerability is an incomplete fix for CVE-2024-1794; exploitation requires that the Forminator form's File Upload field is left at plugin defaults (no 'custom-files' restriction configured) and that the server maps no Content-Type to the .rtx extension — the default behavior of the Debian/Ubuntu Apache package used by the official WordPress Docker image and many shared hosts.

alerts.description: parse5 7.0.0 before 8.1.1 contains an uncaught exception vulnerability in Preprocessor#_processSurrogate that allows remote attackers to crash applications by supplying two consecutive low surrogates. Attackers can submit input such as U+DC00 U+DC00, which decodes to out-of-range code point 0x110000 and throws a RangeError from parse, parseFragment, or streaming parsers, crashing Node.js processes.

@scalar/typebox before 0.1.4 contains a code injection vulnerability in TypeCompiler that allows attackers to execute JavaScript by supplying crafted schema strings. Attackers can inject single-quote breakouts into string format, Kind names, property keys or Literal values to run arbitrary JavaScript in the host Node.js process during Compile() and Check().

NLTK (Natural Language Toolkit) is a suite of open source Python modules, data sets, and tutorials supporting research and development in Natural Language Processing. From 3.10.3 until 3.10.4, the NLTK 3.10.3 JVM hardening validates Java launcher tokens in the options channel but appends the caller-controlled cmd sequence without requiring its first token to be a main class. Supplying -jar or an @argfile through nltk.internals.java or StanfordSegmenter.java_class can therefore execute attacker-selected Java bytecode without the unsafe-JAR opt-in. This issue is fixed in version 3.10.4.

pREST (PostgreSQL REST) is an API that delivers an application on top of a Postgres database. Prior to 2.4.0, the vulnerable parameter is _groupby, handled by GroupByClause in adapters/postgres/postgres.go. adapters/postgres/postgres.go uses the weaker isSafeSQLExpression check for this function-expression branch instead of the stricter single-field validator used for _select. That check validates only the outer function name against a 13-function allowlist and permits nested subqueries, trailing UNION syntax, and inner pg_ functions. controllers/crud.go concatenates the GROUP BY expression while parameterizing only WHERE values, allowing attacker-controlled SQL structure into the clause. Default configuration permits unauthenticated access; a restricted installation may require a low-privilege table reader. UNION-based extraction requires compatible column counts and types and was not verified end to end, but a delay-producing function can cause denial of service without that alignment. This issue is fixed in 2.4.0.

@fastify/reply-from is a Fastify plugin that forwards requests to an upstream HTTP server. In versions before 12.8.4, its buildURL function rejects parent-directory path segments by an exact string match, so a segment that carries a semicolon path parameter, such as a dot-dot segment followed by a semicolon and an optional parameter, is not equal to the plain dot-dot form and passes the traversal check, and the WHATWG URL parser keeps it as an ordinary segment so the base-prefix containment check also passes. Backends that strip semicolon path parameters before resolving dot-segments, such as Apache Tomcat, Jetty, WildFly, and Spring Boot, turn the segment back into a parent-directory reference and resolve it, so an unauthenticated client can escape the intended upstream prefix and reach internal paths such as admin or internal API endpoints, including with state-changing methods. Deployments that proxy to Node.js, nginx, or Express upstreams are not affected. The issue is fixed in @fastify/reply-from 12.8.4, and users should upgrade to 12.8.4 or later.

@fastify/http-proxy is a Fastify plugin that proxies HTTP and WebSocket traffic to an upstream server. In versions from 9.0.0 up to but not including 11.6.10, when the plugin is registered with websocket support enabled, it takes every upgraded socket and dispatches the request through the Fastify router before the WebSocket library takes ownership of the socket. Node.js removes its own error listener from the socket before emitting the upgrade event, and the plugin does not attach one of its own during routing, so a socket error such as a client connection reset that arrives before the WebSocket library takes over is unhandled and terminates the Node.js process. The error window is open whenever anything asynchronous runs between dispatch and the route handler, such as an async hook on the proxied route or any unrelated async route in the application. A single unauthenticated upgrade request followed by a connection reset is enough to crash the server, and it can be repeated to keep the process down. The issue is fixed in @fastify/http-proxy 11.6.10, and users should upgrade to 11.6.10 or later.

@fastify/http-proxy is a Fastify plugin that proxies HTTP and WebSocket traffic to an upstream server. In versions from 9.4.0 up to but not including 11.6.10, when the plugin is registered with websocket support enabled, a WebSocket upgrade request whose path carries a URL fragment is matched by the router and answered with a successful upgrade before the upstream link is created. Building the upstream target then throws, the error is only logged, and the accepted client socket is left open with no error listener, so the next frame the client sends becomes an unhandled error and terminates the Node.js process. A request target that is not a valid URL reference reaching a parameterized prefix triggers the same path. A single unauthenticated upgrade request followed by one frame is enough to crash the server, and it can be repeated to keep the process down. The issue is fixed in @fastify/http-proxy 11.6.10, and users should upgrade to 11.6.10 or later.

RepoManager is a self-hosted deb/rpm package repository. Prior to 5.13.3, a registered host or a party with its host/API credential can submit package metadata. Inventory reporting accepts package name and version, while available-update reporting accepts package name, version, and repository; the repository field exists only on that path. RepoManager stores these values, and stored values are rendered on the host's package detail page without preventing stored HTML or JavaScript from executing. An administrator must later view the page for script execution. The script runs in the administrator's authenticated browser session and can expose administrative data or forge privileged requests; the advisory describes possible escalation through admin-only functionality. Fixed in 5.13.3.

@fastify/http-proxy is a Fastify plugin that proxies HTTP and WebSocket traffic to an upstream server. In versions from 9.0.0 up to but not including 11.6.10, when the plugin is registered with websocket support enabled, a WebSocket upgrade that is pipelined behind another HTTP request on the same cleartext connection arrives while that request's response is still attached to the socket. The shared upgrade listener sees the socket is already claimed and returns early without taking the upgrade, but it does not attach an error listener to the raw socket, and Node.js has already removed its own error listener before emitting the upgrade event. A later socket error on that connection, such as a client connection reset, is therefore unhandled and terminates the Node.js process. A single unauthenticated connection that pipelines an upgrade behind a normal request and then resets is enough to crash the server, and it can be repeated to keep the process down. Upgrades over TLS are not affected. The issue is fixed in @fastify/http-proxy 11.6.10, and users should upgrade to 11.6.10 or later.

In Splunk SOAR versions below 8.8.0, a user with edit permission for a container or workbook task could store attacker-controlled Hypertext Markup Language (HTML) in a note. netty-incubator-codec-ohttp implements Oblivious HTTP (OHTTP) gateway and client functionality using Netty. BinaryHttpParser.readFieldSection then leaves fieldSectionLength unchanged and repeats the loop because its forward-progress checks are Java assertions, which are normally disabled in production. A remote peer that sends a known-length Binary HTTP header or trailer section ending at that boundary can make the parser spin indefinitely and pin the Netty event-loop or worker thread responsible for the channel. netty-incubator-codec-ohttp implements Oblivious HTTP (OHTTP) gateway and client functionality using Netty. A corrupt field line can consume more bytes than its understated declared section length and drive the counter negative, or a truncated field line can return without consuming data and leave the parser in the same state. An unauthenticated OHTTP peer can encrypt such Binary HTTP content under the gateway public configuration, reach OHttpRequestResponseContext.ContentDecoder.decodeChunk, and permanently pin a Netty event-loop thread at full CPU before application business logic. isomorphic-git is a pure JavaScript implementation of Git for Node.js and browsers. Prior to 1.38.7, tree-entry validation in src/models/GitTree.js does not reject the Windows NTFS reserved pathname alias .git::$INDEX_ALLOCATION. When clone() or checkout materializes an attacker-controlled tree containing this alias on Windows using an NTFS filesystem, the alias resolves to the active .git directory and permits writes to trusted repository metadata instead of a normal worktree directory. A malicious repository or object stream can therefore poison repository configuration, hooks, refs, attributes, or other gitdir state. Strict hosting that rejects hasDotgit objects can block the crafted tree, and non-NTFS systems do not interpret the pathname as the active gitdir. isomorphic-git performs the gitdir write but does not itself execute the written hook or configuration; a later native Git or compatible-tool action, such as processing a poisoned core.fsmonitor value, can execute configured commands as the victim developer or CI identity. This issue is fixed in version 1.38.7.

isomorphic-git is a pure JavaScript implementation of Git for Node.js and browsers. Prior to 1.38.8, git cherry-pick applies tree changes through applyTreeChanges in src/utils/walkerToTreeEntryMap.js without checking whether a leading path component is a symbolic link. If a victim worktree contains a tracked symlink to a location outside the worktree and a cherry-picked tree places a file beneath that path, the write follows the symlink and materializes attacker-controlled blob content at the external destination. This allows arbitrary file writes and can cause data tampering, code injection into interpreted files, privilege escalation, denial of service, or follow-on code execution depending on the selected target path. This issue is fixed in version 1.38.8.
